causalModel.founding: Argonians die in the Rose and their bones must reach the dirt; the Chainbreakers built a station near the Blackrose road to receive them.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: A dry rise between the Prison road and the tracks east to the villages, where the Rose's people will hand a body to the villages' people.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: The Rose's families release the dead here for a fee they call a carriage charge; the Chainbreakers pay it and record every payment.
causalModel.pressures: The fee is the most resented transaction in the south, but both sides need it to continue.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: The Rose refusing to release the dead would end the arrangement and put the Chainbreakers and the families in open conflict.

districts.notes: A thatched handover shelter on a low dry rise, with the keeper's hut beside it and a way leaving on each side.

why.what: The rise, the handover shelter on it and the keeper's hut.
why.whyHere: The rise lies between the Prison road and the tracks east to the villages, so both parties can reach it without entering the other's ground.
why.whySpot: The flattest part of the rise, levelled under the shelter.
why.whyNeighbours: Blackrose stands 300 m to the north-west and the Rose 500 m to the south-west. The ferry stage and the bonded stores lie to the north-east.
why.playerPurpose: The handover of the dead, the fee and the record of it.
why.microGeography: Firm, gently sloping grassland, drier than the marsh to the west.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its open front faces north onto the two ways, which end at its two front corners: the Rose's way at the west corner and the villages' way at the east corner.

why.what: The handover shelter: a thatched half pavilion on log posts, open at the front.
why.whyHere: The dead change hands under one roof, in sight of both parties.
why.whySpot: On a pad of levelled earth at the top of the rise.
why.whyNeighbours: The keeper's hut stands a short walk east, on the villages' side.
why.playerPurpose: Where the Rose's dead are received, tagged and wrapped for the road home.
why.microGeography: Trodden earth under thatch, with a row of candles across the floor between the two halves.

playerPurpose.note: The handover of the Rose's dead, the tags and the wrapping for the road home.

why.what: The keeper's hut: a bamboo store hut on short stilts, where the Chainbreakers' keeper holds the carriers' stores and writes down every fee paid.
why.whyHere: On the villages' side of the shelter, which is the Chainbreakers' charge.
why.whySpot: On a levelled pad north-east of the shelter, above the villages' way.
why.whyNeighbours: The shelter is a short walk south-west; the track east starts below the door.
why.playerPurpose: The keeper, the ledger of carriage charges and the carriers' stores.
why.microGeography: A bamboo hut on a mud pad, with a wicker table and chairs outside the door.

playerPurpose.note: The keeper's ledger of carriage charges, kept at the table by the door: every fee paid at the shelter, by date, name and amount.
The Chainbreakers' stores for the carriers: barrels, dried fish and wine.

routes.why: The end of the track from the villages, run on past the keeper's hut to the east corner of the shelter.
A short path up from the villages' way to the keeper's door.
The way the Rose's porters use, from the shelter's west corner down the slope toward the Prison road.

questSockets.why: Where the procession for the dead of White Rose Prison stops: the bones change hands here before the road home.

approaches.sequence: Coming west along the track from the villages, the keeper's hut shows first on the rise, then drops behind the slope, then the thatch of the shelter appears beyond it with the candles under it.
approaches.wayfinding: The track ends below the keeper's door; the shelter stands a short walk west.

approaches.sequence: Coming off the Prison road across the grass, the shelter's thatch shows on the rise, then the way, then the brazier and the bench at its west corner.
approaches.wayfinding: A worn way climbs from the north-west to the shelter's west corner.

networkTerminals.why: The track from the villages to the east ends here, below the keeper's door.

combatSpaces.why: Open grass on all sides of the shelter and the hut.

scaleGrounding.why: The tag-keeper works and sleeps at the shelter and keeps the stores in the hut; the Rose's porters and the villages' carriers come and go.

candidates.why: The plotted anchor's own rise: dry firm ground 3 m above the water table, where the place's track from the villages already ends, with room on its west side for a way down toward the Prison road.
The record's near point, beside the Rose causeway south of Blackrose.
candidates.rejectedBecause: It lies inside the Blackrose disc after the 2026-09-20 island reseat, so the record was moved to this rise.
